changed.title: Small cases only: on the one-a-side n by n promise, n >= 3, an AND/OR/NOT circuit of s gates gives an AND/OR one of at most s + 2n - 5 gates
changed.statement: ∀ (n s : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), 3 ≤ n → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → C.size ≤ s → PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (s + (2 * n - 5))
changed.unlocks: settles this statement on the record; whichever side is proved is kept
changed.context: Truth unknown; our support is small cases only. A circuit with NOT gates right on the promise is turned into one without, paying at most 2n - 5 more gates. The exclusive-OR graph shows the slope cannot be lower: 4 gates with NOT against exactly 2n - 1 without, a gap of 2n - 5. At side 3 the bound is 1 above; a 3 by 3 graph costing 6 with NOT gates and 8 or more without would break it. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
changed.sketch: Merge duplicate lines. Restriction costs no gates. Restoring a line costs at most one OR. In the reduced r by c table, two unread lines in a bank would match. At least r+c-2 raw wires reach the output, requiring r+c-3 binary gates. At that budget the source is positive. One gate higher, a live NOT forces a tree with one use per wire and one omitted line per bank. On mask 14303 only full lines can be omitted. Derive a terminal NOT by polarity: a six-gate source would give a five-gate complement, below its checked minimum of six. Then tackle larger budgets.

changed.title: A short list of vertex sign probes retains a uniform absolute sum margin after adversarial trimming
changed.statement:
∃ C : ℕ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (t k : ℕ), 2 ≤ t → 0 < k →
  let T := Fin t
  let E := {p : T × T // p.1 < p.2}
  ∃ (d : ℕ) (pin : Fin d → T → Bool),
    0 < d ∧ d ≤ C*k*(1+Nat.log 2 t) ∧
    ∀ (v : E → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin d)),
      let norm := Real.sqrt (∑ e : E, (v e)^2)
      let sgn := fun (i : Fin d) (j : T) => if pin i j then (1 : ℝ) else -1
      let a := fun i => |∑ e : E, v e * sgn i e.val.1 * sgn i e.val.2|
      (∑ e : E, |v e|) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt (k : ℝ) * norm →
      400*S.card ≤ d →
      (d : ℝ)*norm + 256*(∑ i ∈ S, a i) ≤ 128*(∑ i, a i)
changed.unlocks: Supplies the error margin needed to reconstruct the entire edge set from a corrupted list of fixed boundary pin counts.
changed.context: Use uniform independent vertex signs in each row. Distinct edge characters are orthogonal. At unit Euclidean norm their quadratic has fourth norm at most 3, hence mean absolute value at least 1/9. The mean of (abs-10) positive part is at most 1/40. Symmetrization and contraction control both empirical means within 1/1024 on the whole stated cone using the maximum of the signed column sums. The largest d/400 coordinates cost at most 10d/400 plus the total excess. Subtract that cost twice and rescale.

changed.title: The exact anchored rank of two layers of binary products for every fixed list of preparation masks
changed.statement:
let F := ZMod 2
∀ (s k : ℕ) (a b : Fin s → Fin k → F) (d : Fin s → F),
  let V := (Fin s → Fin 2 → F) × ((Fin k → F) × (Fin k → F))
  let g := fun (i : Fin s) (x y : V) => ∑ p : Fin 2, x.1 i p * y.1 i p
  let val := fun (x y : V) =>
    (∑ h : Fin k,
      (x.2.1 h + y.2.1 h + ∑ i : Fin s, a i h * g i x y) *
      (x.2.2 h + y.2.2 h + ∑ i : Fin s, b i h * g i x y)) +
      ∑ i : Fin s, d i * g i x y
  let X : Matrix V V F := fun x y => val x y + val x 0 + val 0 y + val 0 0
  let active := fun i : Fin s => a i ≠ 0 ∨ b i ≠ 0
  let edges := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin s × Fin s)).filter (fun h =>
    h.1 < h.2 ∧ (∑ j, (a h.1 j * b h.2 j + b h.1 j * a h.2 j)) ≠ 0)
  X.rank = 2*k + 4*(Finset.univ.filter active).card +
    2*(Finset.univ.filter (fun i => ¬ active i ∧ d i ≠ 0)).card + 4*edges.card
changed.unlocks: If the mask interactions can be maximized, this computes the largest anchored rank attainable with prescribed nonlinear budgets in the two layers.
changed.context: Expand in squarefree monomials on each cube; subset evaluation is invertible and anchoring removes pure terms. The fresh operand coordinates give k invertible two-by-two blocks. For each prepared coordinate the single and its products with fresh bits give an arrow matrix of rank two when its activation vector is nonzero, or of rank one for direct-only use. Distinct prepared coordinates give isolated diagonal monomials precisely when their symplectic pairing is one. Two coordinates per signal give four per paired signal pair.

changed.title: One adaptive phase query after d fixed determinant queries recovers every complex matching product
changed.statement:
∀ (n q : ℕ) (H : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (ζ : ℂ), 0 < n → IsPrimitiveRoot ζ q →
  let I := Fin n
  let E := I × I
  let V := Submodule.span ℚ {v : E → ℚ | ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm I, (∀ j, H (σ j) j = true) ∧
    v = fun e => if σ e.2 = e.1 then (1 : ℚ) else 0}
  let d := Module.finrank ℚ V
  let W := Equiv.Perm I → ℂ
  let S := E → Fin q
  let fits := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) => ∀ i j, H i j = false → A i j = 0
  let w := fun (A : Matrix I I ℂ) (π : Equiv.Perm I) => ∏ j : I, A (π j) j
  let eval := fun (s : S) (A : Matrix I I ℂ) =>
    Matrix.det (fun i j => A i j * ζ ^ (s (i,j)).val : Matrix I I ℂ)
  n * (n ^ d) ^ 2 < q →
  ∃ (front : Fin d → S) (last : (Fin d → ℂ) → S) (read : (Fin d → ℂ) → ℂ → W),
    ∀ A : Matrix I I ℂ, fits A →
      let y := fun h : Fin d => eval (front h) A
      read y (eval (last y) A) = w A
changed.unlocks: Identifies every matching product from rank-many fixed determinant replies and a single final phase evaluation chosen from those replies.
changed.context: Use the bounded list for the d replies. Two distinct candidate vectors give a nonzero signed difference polynomial in the entry phases: different permutations use different monomials of degree n. On the qth-root grid each pair collides on at most n/q of the points. Sum over at most choose(n^d,2) pairs and fix a phase pattern avoiding them all for that list. Read the unique candidate giving the final answer. Empty lists need only a default decoder.

changed.title: Semantic lower bound on key summaries for consecutive output bits of the cyclic column rule with variable public masks
changed.statement:
∀ (k t h : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), 7 ≤ k → k % 3 ≠ 0 → 0 < h → h ≤ k →
  let W := Fin k → ZMod 2
  let ix := fun n : ℕ => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val+k-(s % k)))
  let mix := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x i + x (ix (i.val+2)) + rot 2 x i
  let run := fun (key name : W) (c : Fin (t+1) → W) =>
    (List.finRange (t+1)).foldl (fun (state : W) (j : Fin (t+1)) =>
      let y := mix state
      fun i : Fin k => y i + (1+y (ix (i.val+1)))*y (ix (i.val+2)) +
        rot (3*(j.val+1)+1) key i + c j i) (rot 3 key + name)
  ∀ (start : Fin k) (N : ℕ) (tag : W → Fin N) (bias : W → Fin h → ZMod 2)
    (decode : Fin N → W → (Fin (t+1) → W) → Fin h → ZMod 2),
    (∀ (key name : W) (c : Fin (t+1) → W) (a : Fin h),
      run key name c (ix (start.val+a.val)) = bias key a + decode (tag key) name c a) →
    2^(min k (h+1+5*t)) ≤ N
changed.unlocks: Tests whether a key summary can be shared across names and public masks even when a single scheduled bit survives.
changed.context: Equal tags force each tested difference constant over the public words. The name or latest common mask lets the mixed base vary freely since the spacing-two mix is invertible. Varying the two product operands forces mixed differences zero on h+1 sites. A zero mixed difference at p one step later sums three updates at p−2,p,p+2. Their six operand sites are distinct, so varying each separately forces all six preceding mixed differences zero from p−1 to p+4. Iterate t times. The initial rotated mix is bijective, so the resulting cyclic interval realizes all its bit patterns.

changed.title: A marked-site trace recurrence evaluates the one-query whole-word hit count on singular spacing-two banks
changed.statement:
∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t),
  letI : ∀ p : Prop, Decidable p := Classical.propDecidable
  let F := ZMod 2
  let n := 6*t
  let W := Fin n → F
  let ix := fun j : ℕ => (⟨j % n, Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.zero_lt_succ 5) ht)⟩ : Fin n)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (w : W) (i : Fin n) => w (ix (i.val + n - s % n))
  let out := fun (name c raw : W) (i : Fin n) =>
    let old := rot 3 raw + name
    let y := fun j : Fin n => old j + old (ix (j.val+2)) + old (ix (j.val+n-2))
    y i + (1+y (ix (i.val+1)))*y (ix (i.val+2)) + rot 4 raw i + c i
  let mix := fun (w : W) (i : Fin n) =>
    let old := rot 3 w
    old i + old (ix (i.val+2)) + old (ix (i.val+n-2))
  ∀ name c : W,
    let hits := fun (q : W →ₗ[F] F) (A : F → W →ₗ[F] W) (b : F → W) =>
      Nat.card {w : W // out name c w = A (q w) w + b (q w)}
    let seq := fun (x lo hi : ℤ) =>
      (((!![0,1;-1,x] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ)^t).mulVec ![lo,hi]) 0
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (fixed : Bool), (fixed = true ∨ 240 ≤ t) →
      ((∃ (q : W →ₗ[F] F) (A : F → W →ₗ[F] W) (b : F → W),
        (fixed = true → ∀ w : W, q w = mix w (ix 0)) ∧ k ≤ hits q A b) ↔
        (k : ℤ) ≤ 2*(seq 18 1 13 + seq 6 6 26 + 3 + (6+4*(t : ℤ))*(-1 : ℤ)^t))
changed.unlocks: Gives the whole-word accuracy for one physical site at every width in this family and the unrestricted one-query accuracy beyond the explicit cutoff.
changed.context: For a fixed site, count independent sets omitting it and invert the four checks. Replace its transfer factor by the empty-site matrix J. Each six-site class obeys its trace recurrence. Rotation averages the omitted-site contribution over six sites. The four classes have initial pairs (1,13),(6,26),(3,3),(6,-10) with traces 18,6,2,-2. Translate the other answer coset, doubling the total. The optimizer classification handles an unrestricted question at the stated widths. Full sketch in barriers/statements/probe-flats/one-query-whole-hits.sketch.txt.

changed.title: Two alternating stop positions classify one-round passing-name sets under all physical XOR translations
changed.statement:
∀ (k h d start : Nat) (hk : 0 < k), 0 < d → 0 < h → h+2+2*d ≤ k →
  let W := Fin k → Bool
  let ix := fun i : Nat => (⟨i % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let add := fun (x y : W) (p : Fin k) => xor (x p) (y p)
  let mix := fun (gap : Nat) (x : W) (p : Fin k) =>
    xor (xor (x (ix (p.val + k - gap % k))) (x p)) (x (ix (p.val + gap)))
  let step := fun (z : W) (p : Fin k) =>
    xor (z p) (!(z (ix (p.val+1))) && z (ix (p.val+2)))
  let accepts := fun (offset : W) (z : Nat → Bool) (u : W) =>
    ∀ j : Fin h, step (mix d (add u offset)) (ix (start+j.val)) = z j.val
  let stop := fun (z : Nat → Bool) (lane : Nat) =>
    let m := (h-lane)/2
    ((List.range m).filter (fun t => z (h-1-lane-2*t))).headD m
  ∀ (offset₀ offset₁ : W) (z₀ z₁ : Nat → Bool),
    let shifts := (Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun delta =>
      ∀ u : W, accepts offset₀ z₀ u ↔ accepts offset₁ z₁ (add u delta))
    shifts.card = if stop z₀ 0 = stop z₁ 0 ∧ stop z₀ 1 = stop z₁ 1
      then 2^(k-(h+2)) else 0
changed.unlocks: gives the exact test and number of translations between two physical passing-name sets
changed.context: Write the two tail bits as s,t. From output z recover y[j]=z[j]+(1+z[j+1])y[j+2] before the final row. Its four strips form a translate of sA+tB+(1+s)tC. B marks the last site. A and C mark alternating suffixes ending at h and h-1, stopping at their first guard one. The last three coordinates distinguish the basis of the difference span, so translations preserve both suffixes. The four points are affinely independent, hence have no nonzero translation period. Lift the unique mixed shift through the uniform mixer.

changed.title: Subcubic pigeonhole proof lengths up to the logarithmic girth threshold at every large edge count
changed.statement:
∃ C N₀ : ℕ, 2 ≤ C ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N →
  let ell := Nat.clog 2 N
  ∀ h : ℕ, C ≤ h → h ≤ ell →
    ∃ q : ℕ, ∃ G : PEqualNP.Expanders.BipGraph (q+1) q,
      Fintype.card (PEqualNP.Expanders.GEdge G) = N ∧
      (∀ u, 2 ≤ (G u).card ∧ (G u).card ≤ 3) ∧
      (∀ v, 2 ≤ (PEqualNP.Expanders.rightNbrs G v).card ∧
        (PEqualNP.Expanders.rightNbrs G v).card ≤ 3) ∧

changed.title: Two-batch affine search with prescribed witness probes has an exact cover criterion using the permitted forms
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (n k t m d e : ℕ),
  let X := Fin n → K
  let U := Fin k → K
  let Y := Fin t → K
  let Z := X × U
  let W := U →ₗ[K] K
  ∀ (P : AffineSubspace K X) (bad : Fin m → AffineSubspace K X)
    (M : Fin m → U →ₗ[K] Y) (A B : Set W),
    let legal := fun (S : Set W) (f : Z →ₗ[K] K) =>
      f.comp (LinearMap.inr K X U) = 0 ∨ f.comp (LinearMap.inr K X U) ∈ S
    (∃ x : X, x ∈ P) →
    ((∃ (ask : Fin d → Z →ₗ[K] K) (next : (Fin d → K) → Fin e → Z →ₗ[K] K)
        (out : (Fin d → K) → (Fin e → K) → Fin m × Y),
      (∀ j, legal A (ask j)) ∧ (∀ z j, legal B (next z j)) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ P, ∀ u : U,
        let z := fun j => ask j (x,u)
        let a := out z (fun j => next z j (x,u))
        x ∉ bad a.1 ∧ a.2 = M a.1 u) ↔
    ∃ (g : ℕ) (Q : Finset W) (S : Fin g → Finset (Fin m)) (R : Fin g → Finset W),
      0 < g ∧ (∀ f ∈ Q, f ∈ A) ∧ Q.card + (g-1) ≤ d ∧
      (∀ j, (S j).Nonempty ∧ (∀ f ∈ R j, f ∈ B) ∧ (R j).card + ((S j).card-1) ≤ e ∧
        ∀ i ∈ S j, ∀ u : U, (∀ f ∈ Q, f u = 0) → (∀ f ∈ R j, f u = 0) → M i u = 0) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ P, ∃ j, ∃ i ∈ S j, x ∉ bad i)

changed.title: Exact polynomial-calculus span at the degree of generic binary linear projection tests
changed.statement:
∀ m k : ℕ,
  let I := Fin m
  let J := Fin k
  let K := ZMod 2
  let V := I × Option J
  let P := MvPolynomial V K
  let Mask := Finset I
  let T := {U : Mask // U.Nonempty ∧ U.card ≤ k+1}
  let profile := fun (S : Mask) (U : T) => if U.val ⊆ S then (1 : K) else 0
  let part := fun (S : Mask) (j : Option J) => ∑ i ∈ S, (MvPolynomial.X (i,j) : P)
  let test := fun S : Mask => part S none * ∏ j : J, (1 + part S (some j))
  let bools : Set P := Set.range (fun v : V => MvPolynomial.X v * MvPolynomial.X v + MvPolynomial.X v)
  let axioms := fun (H : Finset Mask) => bools ∪ Set.image test (H : Set Mask)
  (∀ (H : Finset Mask) (S : Mask),
    PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCDerivable (axioms H) (k+1) (test S) ↔
      profile S ∈ Submodule.span K (Set.image profile (H : Set Mask))) ∧
  (∀ b : ℕ, (∃ H : Finset Mask, H.card ≤ b ∧
    ∀ S, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCDerivable (axioms H) (k+1) (test S)) ↔
    (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k+1), m.choose (j+1)) ≤ b) ∧
  ∀ (H : Finset Mask) (low : Mask → P),
    LinearIndependent K (fun S : H => profile S.val) →
    (∀ S ∈ H, (low S).totalDegree ≤ k) →
    ∀ p : P, p.totalDegree ≤ k →
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCDerivable
        (bools ∪ Set.image (fun S => test S + low S) (H : Set Mask)) (k+1) p →
      ∀ x : V → K, MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0
changed.unlocks: Determines the exact size advantage of semantic row pooling over deriving every original short-row axiom at its own degree.
changed.context: Expand each test by the row support of its monomials. Each nonempty support through size k+1 occurs in a square-free top monomial, one variable per column counting the constant. Its coefficient in a sum is exactly the containment-profile entry. A profile relation cancels the whole unperturbed sum. In a critical-degree PC proof a multiplication can start only from a lower-degree line, whose evaluation in this span must vanish. Lower perturbations preserve that obstruction for independent profiles. Short masks give a triangular containment basis.

changed.title: A quadratic-time binary transducer emits the four-uniform pairing list directly and preserves every ternary solution
changed.statement:
let bits := fun (w v : Nat) => (List.range w).map (fun j => v.testBit j)
let header := fun n : Nat => List.replicate n true ++ [false]
let width := fun n : Nat => n.log2+1
let Ban := (Nat × Nat) × (Nat × Nat)
let legal := fun (n : Nat) (B : List Ban) => 2 ≤ n ∧ ∀ e ∈ B,
  e.1.1 < e.2.1 ∧ e.2.1 < n ∧ e.1.2 < 3 ∧ e.2.2 < 3
let enc := fun (n : Nat) (B : List Ban) =>
  header n ++ B.flatMap (fun e => bits (width n) e.1.1 ++ bits 2 e.1.2 ++
    bits (width n) e.2.1 ++ bits 2 e.2.2)
let valid := fun (n : Nat) (B : List Ban) (a : Fin n → Fin 3) =>
  let v := List.ofFn (fun j => (a j).val)
  ∀ e ∈ B, v.getD e.1.1 3 ≠ e.1.2 ∨ v.getD e.2.1 3 ≠ e.2.2
let pack := fun (k : Nat) (rows : List (List Nat)) =>
  header k ++ rows.flatMap (fun row => row.flatMap (bits (width k)))
let well := fun (k : Nat) (rows : List (List Nat)) => ∀ row ∈ rows,
  row.length = 4 ∧ row.Nodup ∧ ∀ v ∈ row, v < k
let wins := fun (k : Nat) (rows : List (List Nat)) (P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) =>
  Function.Involutive P ∧ ∀ row ∈ rows, ∃ u : Fin k, u.val ∈ row ∧
    (P u).val ∈ row ∧ P u ≠ u
let emit := fun (n : Nat) (B : List Ban) =>
  let flag := fun (i c : Nat) => [8*i+2+2*c,8*i+3+2*c]
  let block := fun (i : Nat) =>
    [[8*i,8*i+2,8*i+4,8*i+6]] ++ (List.range 3).flatMap (fun c =>
      (List.range 2).flatMap (fun b => (List.range 4).map (fun j =>
        [8*i+b] ++ flag i c ++ [8*((i+1)%n)+j])))
  (List.range n).flatMap block ++ B.map (fun e => flag e.1.1 e.1.2 ++ flag e.2.1 e.2.2)
∃ (f : List Bool → List Bool) (C : Nat),
  (∃ M : Turing.TM2ComputableInTime (fun x : List Bool => x) (fun x : List Bool => x) f,
    (∀ j, Finite (M.tm.Γ j)) ∧ ∀ z, M.time z ≤ C*(z+1)^2) ∧
  (∀ x : List Bool, (¬ ∃ n B, legal n B ∧ enc n B = x) → f x = []) ∧
  ∀ n B, legal n B →
    let k := 8*n+1
    let rows := emit n B
    f (enc n B) = pack k rows ∧ well k rows ∧ rows.length = 25*n+B.length ∧
      (pack k rows).length = k+1+4*(25*n+B.length)*width k ∧
      Nonempty ({a : Fin n → Fin 3 // valid n B a} ≃
        {P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) // wins k rows P})

Then scan the bans, writing two flag endpoints per side by shifting the index three bits and adding its tag. No subset enumeration or duplicate removal is needed. Counters and record scans fit quadratic time in the input length, including reversing the output. The local selector and sealed-block correspondence give the bijection after forgetting duplicates.

changed.title: A polynomial-size fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit counts universal key shifts for joint output parities
changed.statement:
∀ (k r m : Nat), 0 < k →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let state := fun (col : Bool) (w u : Nat) (c : Nat → Fin (2^k)) =>
    let g := if col then 2 else 1
    (List.range r).foldl (fun x j =>
      step (x ^^^ rot g x ^^^ rot (k-g) x) ^^^
        rot (if col then 3*(j+1)+1 else 2*j) w ^^^ (c (j+1)).val)
      (rot (if col then 3 else 1) w ^^^ u)
  let parity := fun (mask x : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun b i => xor b (mask.testBit i && x.testBit i)) false
  let bits := fun (n x : Nat) => (List.range n).map (fun i => x.testBit i)
  let bank := fun (A : Fin m → Fin (2^k)) =>
    (List.finRange m).flatMap (fun j => bits k (A j).val)
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (2*m*k+m+2*k+(k+1)) C ∧
    C.size ≤ 2^20 * (r+1) * (k+m+1)^8 ∧
    ∀ (A B : Fin m → Fin (2^k)) (y : Fin m → Bool)
      (pin value : Fin (2^k)) (t : Fin (2^(k+1))),
      let good := fun (d : Fin (2^k)) =>
        (d.val &&& pin.val) = (value.val &&& pin.val) ∧
        ∀ (w u v : Fin (2^k)) (cr cc : Nat → Fin (2^k)) (j : Fin m),
          let w' := w.val ^^^ d.val
          let dr := state false w' u.val cr ^^^ state false w.val u.val cr
          let dc := state true w' v.val cc ^^^ state true w.val v.val cc
          xor (parity (A j).val dr) (parity (B j).val dc) = y j
      C.eval (bank A ++ bank B ++ List.ofFn y ++ bits k pin.val ++ bits k value.val ++
        bits (k+1) t.val) = decide (t.val ≤ Nat.card {d : Fin (2^k) // good d})

changed.title: Affine matching tests recover loss on regular graphs with a sharp tolerance attained by single OR gates
changed.statement:
∀ (F : Type) [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F],
  let q := Fintype.card F
  ∀ e : F ≃ Fin q,
    let G := F → F → Bool
    let Circ := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit
    let line := fun (a b x y : F) => decide (y = a*x+b)
    let tab := fun (C : Circ) (x y : F) => C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach (e x) (e y))
    let cells := (Finset.univ : Finset (F × F))
    let area := fun (C : Circ) => (cells.filter (fun z => tab C z.1 z.2)).card
    let loss := fun (C : Circ) (T : G) => (cells.filter (fun z => tab C z.1 z.2 ≠ T z.1 z.2)).card
    let excess := fun {m : ℕ} (D : Fin m → Circ) (w : Fin m → ℝ) (d : ℕ) (T : G) =>
      ∑ i, w i * ((loss (D i) T : ℝ) - (q : ℝ)*(d : ℝ) - (1-2*(d : ℝ)/(q : ℝ))*(area (D i) : ℝ))
    let single := fun (x y : F) => (⟨[⟨.or, [(e x).val, q+(e y).val]⟩], q+q⟩ : Circ)
    ∀ (t : ℕ) (T : G),
      (∀ x, (Finset.univ.filter (fun y => T x y)).card = t) →
      (∀ y, (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => T x y)).card = t) →
      let n := fun (a b : F) => (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => T x (a*x+b))).card
      let low := fun (a : F) => Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty (n a)
      let slopes := (Finset.univ : Finset F).erase 0
      let K := ∑ a ∈ slopes, (t-low a)
      (∀ (m : ℕ) (D : Fin m → Circ) (w : Fin m → ℝ),
        (∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) → (∑ i, w i) = 1 →
        let E := excess D w
        E t T = (∑ a ∈ slopes, ∑ b, ((n a b - low a : ℕ) : ℝ)*E 1 (line a b))/(q : ℝ) ∧
        ∀ h : ℝ, 0 ≤ h → (∀ a ∈ slopes, ∀ b, E 1 (line a b) ≤ h) → E t T ≤ (K : ℝ)*h) ∧
      ∃ D : Fin (q^3) → Circ, (∀ i, ∃ x y, D i = single x y) ∧
        let E := excess D (fun _ => 1/(q : ℝ)^3)
        let h := 2/(q : ℝ)^3
        (∀ a ∈ slopes, ∀ b, E 1 (line a b) ≤ h) ∧
        (∃ a ∈ slopes, ∃ b, E 1 (line a b) = h) ∧ E t T = (K : ℝ)*h

An equality removes this graph from the search for a saving.
